products.title: Armchair - Zefir - By Studiopepe
products.description_html: With Zefir, Studiopepe combines design with artisanal mastery to craft an artwork that boasts a strong and distinctive presence. A tribute to lightness, this chair with its curved T-shaped backrest catches the eye with its perfect balance of geometric rigour and sinuous lines. Crafted from matt black metal, the unique backrest structure ascends like a graphic signature that shapes the space, softly embracing the guest. The leather upholstery, soft to the touch and made entirely by hand, transforms everyday comfort into an aesthetic and sensual statement. Zefir enriches the scene with its subtle balance between strength and grace, leaving a distinctive impression of strong personality.

products.title: Armchair - T Chair - By Federico Peri
products.description_html: The T Chair by Federico Peri is a minimalist design marvel, seamlessly merging practicality with understated elegance. The chair's geometric design is characterized by the distinctive 'T' shape of its padded backrest, an iconic feature that embraces the user, providing both comfort and personality to the design while imparting a sense of security and robustness. The seat's structure, crafted in polished glossy or matt black brushed wiredrawn aluminium, is welded at sharp angles and harmonizes with the inviting padding of the cushions, creating a captivating visual contrast. With its sober and decisive style, T Chair is a versatile piece of furniture, perfect to complete any environment, from the contemporary living room to the most formal dining room.

products.title: Armchair - Stig - By Roberto Lazzeroni
products.description_html: Stig is a leather-covered chair whose design, by Roberto Lazzeroni, is inspired by the ironic furniture designed by Jean Royère. The chair’s distinguishing element is the base that becomes a sculpture and makes this small work of cabinet-making unique and immediately recognisable. It is a solid, thick sled made of wenge ash which, when raised, supports the seat and backrest. The two leather-covered cushions rest lightly on the structure and invite you to experience the unusual comfort of this statuesque piece.

products.title: Armchair - So Far - By Studiopepe
products.description_html: Studiopepe's So Far chairs, with their luxurious upholstery, pay homage to an iconic design by blending 1970s influences with a modern elegance that feels as welcoming as an embrace. The tubular metal structure defines a bold and distinctive stage presence, which harmoniously dialogues with the soft and enveloping lines of the oversized seats. The combination of metal (available in hand-brushed burnished or glossy chrome finishes) and leather-covered cushions expresses a welcoming personality with timeless charm, able to enrich any living environment with style and versatility.

products.title: Armchair - Oslo - By Paola Navone
products.description_html: Exuding minimalism and comfort, the Oslo chairs and stools by Paola Navone feature straightforward geometries that are perfectly complemented by luxurious leather upholstery, achieving an ideal blend of elegance and adaptability. The raw-cut stitching on the upholstery, exclusively available with leather legs, imparts a material sense to each chair and stool. Both functional and iconic, these chairs seamlessly fit into any setting, eliminating the distinctions between the living room, dining area, and workspace.

products.title: Armchair - Nepal - By Paola Navone
products.description_html: The Nepal chair, a bold creation by Paola Navone, redefines the concept of contemporary seating through a compelling contrast of elements: the extraordinary tactile softness of Mongolian fur envelops and embraces, while the solid frame outlines strong, architectural lines within the space. Each Nepal chair becomes a full sensory experience—an island of comfort that captivates at first glance and delights at first touch. The natural upholstery, available in a palette of luminous and vibrant hues, captures and transforms light, creating a magnetic focal point in any setting. Nepal is far more than a furnishing accessory—it is a stylistic statement that transforms its surroundings with exuberant presence; a living sculpture that invites both tactile and visual exploration.

products.title: Armchair - Miss Rope - By Studiopepe
products.description_html: Striking and regal, Miss Rope is the woven paper cord chair by Studiopepe that, with its elongated design and high backrest, evokes the ceremonial seats and tribal thrones of far-off places. The weave draping the metal structure reflects the artisan's handiwork, where meticulous and steady movements bring the creation to life. The vertical lines, reminiscent of sculpture, convey the sitter's significance. Thanks to its expertly hand-crafted cord, Miss Rope is a majestic enhancement to both indoor and outdoor settings, owing to its remarkable resilience against outdoor conditions.

products.title: Armchair - Jodie - By Christophe Delcourt
products.description_html: Taking inspiration from palaver-style seating, the whimsical chairs in Christophe Delcourt's Jodie collection best express the ideal of sharing, inviting guests to lounge and relax. The sinuous roundness of the forms enhances the designer's architectural choice, resulting in a refined interplay that shifts between sturdy, assertive lines and gentle, welcoming structures. The precious leather that covers each chair makes Jodie's sculptural lines extremely comfortable, in a masterpiece of design that provides a memorable seating experience.

products.description_html:
Acclaimed designer Naoto Fukasawa presents his latest exploration of shape and form with Tuscany, the chaise longue that marks an important contribution to the Molteni&C catalog, inspiring new ideas. In creating the design, Fukasawa interpreted the iconic vistas of the Italian landscape through the lens of his own aesthetic, merging stylistic cues in a way that captures the finest of both worlds – the Italian and the Japanese.

The Tuscany embodies the idea of comfort with a structure expertly molded to the contours of the body.

Its silhouette provides a sense of lightness and fluidity rooted in an innovative design that is both visually harmonious and deeply relaxing.

The form is the result of meticulous technical development by Molteni&C's R&D Department, which created, together with the designer, the ideal proportions for the chaise's unique shape. The smooth, rounded legs are made from solid wood and are connected by a satin brass H-frame, providing a sturdy and stylish base for the chaise longue.

Connected to one another by carefully hidden zippers, the cushions form an articulated whole that neatly hugs the structure. These are available in a variety of fabrics and leathers from Molteni&C’s textile collection to easily complement a range of interior concepts. The rounded headrest moves independently from the square cushions and is balanced by a metal dowel held by adjustable straps to hold it in place, allowing for customized comfort.

Tuscany is available in two versions. The first offers a eucalyptus finish with matte painted satin brass. The second is composed of natural Sunrise Oak, for a contemporary balance of bright wood and stainless steel.
Stunning and innovative, the Tuscany chaise longue seamlessly blends form and function, and is sure to become a timeless addition to any interior space.

products.title: Armchair - Continuum D.163.7 - By Gio Ponti
products.description_html:
The Molteni&C Heritage catalog celebrates the addition of the Continuum armchair into the 2024 Collection. Designed by Gio Ponti in 1963, this piece underscores the enduring alliance between Brianza's manufacturing companies, Molteni&C and Bonacina 1889, and the generations of pioneers from within the Italian design furniture sector. These companies are dedicated to preserving their distinctive artisanal skills and long held roots in the region. In the case of the Continuum, such craftsmanship is shown through the expert processing of rattan, a natural material intricately interwoven and curved at every step.

The design of the Continuum armchair aims to materialize a continuous and sinuous brushstroke, inspired by organic forms, elegantly realized through the uninterrupted line flowing from headrest to armrest. The Continuum draws further inspiration from bergères designed in the early 1950s for hotels and cruise ships. Crafted entirely in Italy, the armchair utilizes first-class materials from the rattan family: manao and malacca sourced from the equatorial forests of Indonesia. The structure and backrest are shaped from manao cane by skilled artisans, and each piece demands over 200 hours of meticulous craftsmanship. The seat, crafted from canes with a smaller diameter, is affixed to the structure using special flat rattan cane.

The Continuum features cushioning available in a diverse array of textile and leather finishes. Upon request, the Continuum can be enhanced with a cushion featuring polyurethane foam padding and removable cover.

With this project, Molteni&C reaffirms its commitment to preserving the legacy of Gio Ponti, in collaboration with the Gio Ponti Archives, guardians of the furniture's authenticity. Bonacina, a symbol of Italian excellence celebrating its 135th anniversary this year and renowned for its unique and eclectic style, will guarantee high-quality standards using raw materials and expert craftsmanship, in line with the sustainability policy embraced by both companies.

products.title: Armchair - Round D.154.5 - By Gio Ponti
products.description_html:
The iconic Round D.154.5 designed by Gio Ponti has very modern shapes, almost out of this world, which had never been thought of before.

The early 1950s marked a turning point in Gio Ponti’s furniture designs, towards highly innovative solutions linked to functional and essential shapes: the end of the Second World War, with the desire to restart and rebuild a modern world full of novelties, thus moving away from the past; the availability of innovative materials, which made it possible to conceive objects that were previously unfeasible.

Characterized by avantgarde materials and technologies, such as the Vipla (a plastic material that resembles leather) for the upholstery, curved plywood to join the backrest and seat, and metal feet with non-slip tips that are easy to assemble.

Round (D.154.5) is also referred to as ‘Otto Pezzi’ (Eight Pieces) in the Ponti/Fornaroli/Rosselli study. In fact, there are eight
pieces that make up the chair: backrest, seat, two curved plywood elements and four legs, which screw into the seat to hold the whole thing together.

Designed in 1954, full production began in 1956/1957 and it was officially presented at the 11th Milan Triennale in 1957 (Feal Pavilion), along with other innovative Ponti
furnishings, in a limited number of examples which are now highly sought after by collectors.
